summary: Initial review: no confirmed unauthorized access. The Grafana traversal probes returned 404, the SSH failures are not logins, and the recurring deploy-password sessions are consistent with the old monitor. I found an enabled privileged contractor account missing from the directory and excessive release privileges. I am hardening these and checking live activity and job integrity.

At 17:34:32 a session using Nico’s SSH key ran two complementary sudo find/delete commands on db-01, deleting old and recent backups alike. The DB connection from web-01:53114 correlates with an SSH session from 174.205.16.153. This is destructive activity, not a scan. I’m securing the remaining copies, containing the credential and checking CI.

The first address used nvega’s nv-x13 key through web-01 to erase db-01 backup files. A second, suspected related session used nico@x1-old from 174.205.226.245 on web-01, then the implicated nv-x13 key on ci-01 (matched web source port 38278). No CI archive loss observed. I terminated the sessions, revoked the implicated keys, preserved alternate login methods and narrowed Nico’s sudo privileges on all hosts. I restored 22 DB backup files; the checksums of all 12 nightly archives match the independent CI copies. No evidence so far of a named shop secret being read.
